[EFFECT] The year feature has a sharp, step-change effect on predicted hourly demand: in 2011 it consistently reduces predicted rentals (contribution of about −0.23 in log space), while in 2012 it consistently boosts them (about +0.20 in log space). There is no gradual transition — the model sees a clear jump in the overall demand level from one year to the next, reflecting system-wide growth between the two years.

[IMPORTANCE] With an importance score of 0.217 and a rank of 3rd out of 9 features, the year is one of the strongest drivers of predicted demand in this model, behind only a couple of other features. The gap between 2011 and 2012 represents a substantial shift in the overall scale of rentals.

[RECOMMENDATION] When benchmarking targets or staffing levels, avoid directly comparing 2011 figures to 2012 figures without accounting for this growth — the system-wide demand was substantially higher in 2012, so plans built on 2011 data alone will likely underestimate bike and staff needs.
